topic: Default Initialization of Objects in C++
explanation: In C++, default initialization refers to the process of initializing an object without providing explicit initial values. It determines how objects are initialized when no initializer is specified, which is crucial for understanding object lifetime, constructor invocation, and resource management. Depending on the type—such as class types, arrays, or references—default initialization behaves differently, affecting program correctness and performance. Modern C++ emphasizes understanding default initialization to write safe, efficient, and predictable code.
